newsitem.title: USA: Moody's upgrades Illinois, issues warning on COPs.
newsitem.headline: Moody's upgrades Illinois, issues warning on COPs.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service had some good news and a warning for Illinois on Monday.
The good news was that the ratings on $5.3 billion of Illinois' general obligation debt and $1.6 billion of Build Illinois sales tax revenue bonds were upgraded to Aa3 from A1.
The warning had to with controversy over a $19.2 million 1996 insured certificates of participation issue.

Moody's said it expected continued appropriations on the COPs despite a lawsuit, brought by Democratic state lawmakers, challenging the legality of the issue and remarks by the new chairman of the House Appropriations Committee that the Democrat-controlled House may not make those appropriations.

"Failure to appropriate certificate debt service would cast doubt on the state's willingness to support its debt in general and could have negative rating repercussions for both the state's general obligation and appropriation-derived debt," Moody's said in its credit report.

The rating agency added that it would review Illinois' rating when the fiscal 1998 budget is adopted. An underlying rating of A3 was assigned to the state's outstanding COPs, most of which are insured.

Mike Colsch, Illinois deputy budget director, said payments on the COPs were covered through June 30, the end of the current fiscal year, and that an appropriation would be proposed in the fiscal 1998 budget Republican Gov. Jim Edgar is set to unveil next month.
"We're going to honor our obligations," Colsch said.
He added that the Edgar Administration was pleased with the rating upgrades.
"We've been working towards this for awhile," he said.
Moody's cited Illinois' improved financial condition for the upgrades.

The rating agency pointed to the state's efforts to eliminate a nagging backlog of Medicaid billds, control social services costs, improve ending cash balances, and trim its deficit as measured on a generally accepted accounting principles basis to $1.1 billion at the end of fiscal 1996 from more than $2 billion in fiscal 1993.
The upgrades followed three downgrades of the state by Moody's between 1991 and 1995.
Moody's rating action came in anticipation of a $250 million competitive Illinois sale scheduled for Thursday.
Last week, Standard & Poor's Corp. affirmed the state's AA-minus rating, while Fitch Investors Service confirmed an AA rating.
